name: free_conv_enclosed_and_jackets
title: Natural convection in enclosures and vessels: plates, critical Rayleigh numbers, helical coils, vessel jackets (function library)
summary: Ten EES FUNCTIONs for the natural convection of an enclosed fluid layer, of a helical coil in a tank and of a vessel jacket: the Rayleigh-Benard Nusselt numbers between parallel horizontal plates (Holling-Herwig as its residual, Probert, Hollands with a user-supplied critical Rayleigh number), between vertical plates (Thess, aspect ratio), the critical Rayleigh number of parallel disks (Buell-Caton polynomial), the helical-coil correlations of Ali, Prabhanjan-Rennie-Raghavan and Xin-Ebadian (vertical or horizontal), and the average heat-transfer coefficient of a vessel jacket (Lehrer, Stein-Schmidt, tangential or radial inlet, with or without the buoyancy contribution).
language_features: implicit equation in the main program

authors: M. Hoelling and H. Herwig (Holling-Herwig correlation)
S. D. Probert, R. G. Brooks and M. Dixon (Probert correlation)
M. E. Ali (vertical helical coil correlation)
D. G. Prabhanjan, T. J. Rennie and G. S. V. Raghavan (helical coiled tubes)
R. C. Xin and M. A. Ebadian (helicoidal pipes)
J. C. Buell and I. Catton (critical Rayleigh number of disks)
W. A. Stein and W. Schmidt (jacket side of an agitated vessel)
origin.notes: ht 1.2.0, commit 85e0ee6 (2025-12-07), files ht/conv_free_enclosed.py, ht/conv_free_immersed.py (Nu_coil_Xin_Ebadian) and ht/conv_jacket.py, MIT license, Copyright (C) 2016 Caleb Bell. The scientific basis of each correlation is the original paper or book cited in its function comment block. Translation published under the CoolSolve_Library MIT license (decision D3).

verification.reference: doctest values of ht 1.2.0 ht/conv_free_enclosed.py, ht/conv_free_immersed.py and ht/conv_jacket.py (case A) and additional values computed with the same ht functions in a throw-away virtualenv (case B); 33 output values in total
verification.notes: compare_solution.py: 33 common variables, 0 differ (rtol=0.001); largest relative deviation 8.8e-13 (Nu_HH_B), i.e. round-off only. The two Holling-Herwig residuals are compared against an exact zero and are 2.8e-14 and 7.3e-12 in absolute value.
